preconditions.expression: all(2 <= int(x) <= 100 for x in stdin.split()) and len(stdin.split()) == 3
preconditions.description: Input consists of exactly three integers: n (2 ≤ n ≤ 100), d (|d| ≤ 10^4), and l (1 ≤ l ≤ 100), separated by spaces.
No additional constraints on input beyond stated bounds.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == '-1' or (all(1 <= int(x) <= l for x in stdout.split()) and len(stdout.split()) == n)
postconditions.description: If no valid initial sequence exists, stdout is '-1'. Otherwise, stdout contains exactly n integers between 1 and l (inclusive), representing a valid initial sequence that reduces to d after all operations.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() != '-1' implies (lambda seq: (lambda f: f(f))(lambda rec: lambda: rec() if len(seq) == 1 else rec()(seq[:-2] + [seq[-2] - seq[-1]]))())() == d)
postconditions.description: If stdout is not '-1', the sequence of integers in stdout, when repeatedly reduced by replacing the two rightmost elements with their difference (left - right), eventually yields d as the single remaining element.
